item.title: ‘Tis the Season for Overconsumption
item.description: According to The Journal, Ireland produces up to 30% more waste at Christmas than any other time of the year. As a fashion lover, fast fashion immediately springs to mind as an example of this. We all know by now the damage that fast fashion does. The fashion industry is responsible for 10% of global carbon emissions and 20% of global wastewater, and yet clothing and accessory retailers have their highest sales this time of year. item.title: Louise Kennedy, the Brains Behind Catherine Connolly’s Inauguration Outfit
item.description: Just under a month ago, Catherine Connolly became the tenth president of Ireland. For her inauguration outfit, she opted for a total purple look by celebrated Irish designer Louise Kennedy. In an interview with Her.ie, Connolly expressed her desire to use her voice and role to “enable and empower”. With this intention, the colour of her outfit takes on a more powerful meaning. item.title: Four Films and a TV
item.description: A new addition to The University Times this year, Four Films and a TV, is a very special column giving out very special recommendations. Every month, the editor will be making a list of underappreciated but unparalleled films (four) and (TV) series (one) united by a topical theme, plot device or personality. item.title: The UAE Cuts Scholarship Funding for Emirati Nationals Looking to Study in Trinity
item.description: In early January, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) withdrew scholarship funding opportunities for its citizens at all UK and Irish universities that had previously been offered. This was done in response to what they say to be a rising Muslim Brotherhood influence and promotion of political Islam in university Islamic societies. item.description: History fans around the world have rejoiced at Burns’ new six-part documentary, The American Revolution (2025). Last Tuesday, the first instalment of the series was screened by the DU History Society in Thomas Davis Theatre, and unsurprisingly, it was fantastic. item.title: One Kinda Folk: Review
item.description: A cold November morning called for a coffee and a sweet treat, so I headed with some friends to One Kinda Folk on Leeson St. A short walk from the Charlemont Luas stop, this cosy café offers a plethora of options. The exterior was adorned with seasonal decorations, the large window giving a glimpse of the rustic and inviting interior. item.title: President Mary McAleese Presented with Praeses Elit Award
item.description: This Wednesday, February 25th, former President Mary McAleese was distinguished with the Praeses Elit award by the Trinity Law Society (Law Soc). Mary McAleese is recognised for her “lifelong dedication to bridge building, equality, and compassionate leadership”, which embodies the very spirit of the award, according to the Law Soc Instagram caption. item.title: Columbia Student Detained by Department of Homeland Security in Residential Building
item.description: Today, on February 26th, at 6:30am New York time, federal agents from the United States Department of Homeland Security (DHS) entered a Columbia University residential building and detained a student in the Columbia School of General Studies. The School of General Studies is the school that Dual BA students at Trinity attend in their last two years of the programme.
